I began documenting U.S and world history on February 4, 2025, shortly after Trump’s second term began. What started as an effort to keep a record of the events unfolding around me has grown into 13 journals documenting the political, social, and historical reality of the era I’m living through and everything that led up to this point. Inspired by journalists, independent media, political commentators, historical archives, and the people who refuse to let injustice go unchallenged, I made it my mission to document what I witness, research the evidence, record important statements and events, and preserve the details that could otherwise be forgotten, distorted, or erased with time. My journals cover far more than one president or one political party. They document threats to democracy, political corruption, attacks on civil liberties, racism, systemic oppression, LGBTQ+ rights, immigration, war, genocide, political extremism, propaganda, abuses of power, and the people whose lives are affected by these realities. I also document the history behind these issues, because so much of what happens today cannot be understood without acknowledging what came before it. That includes the ongoing legacy of racial terror in America, from historical lynchings to modern-day cases of suspected racial violence and deaths that raise serious questions about whether justice has been served. Black Americans and other marginalized communities have endured generations of oppression, and I refuse to treat that history as something confined to the past. Claims must be examined through evidence, but uncomfortable questions deserve to be investigated rather than dismissed. I record dates, times, events, sources, photographs, evidence, and my own observations. I revisit information, correct mistakes when necessary, and try to distinguish documented facts from allegations, analysis, and personal opinion. I recognize that no person is entirely free of bias, including me. My responsibility is to take this work seriously, be transparent about my perspective, and pursue the truth as carefully as I can. I am not claiming to be a professional historian. I am an American living through these events who believes that ordinary people have a responsibility to bear witness to their own time. These journals are my personal historical archive, a record of what I witnessed, what I researched, what concerned me, and what I believe future generations deserve the opportunity to examine for themselves. One day, these events will be history. The people who lived through them will grow older, memories will fade, political narratives will change, and some will attempt to rewrite what happened. I want there to be a record of what people were saying, what was happening, what evidence existed, and how this era was experienced by someone who lived through it. Thirteen journals, and I am not finished. This is my contribution to preserving the historical record. Not because my perspective is the only one that matters, but because it deserves to exist alongside the evidence and the voices of others. THE DECAY OF THE AMERICAN NAME. February 4, 2025 — present. #politics #worldhistory #journaltok #documenting #politicalcommentary
